summary: Tested three new features (Player Compare, Value Predictor with OLS, Live Nation Map) end-to-end. Backend: 15 new pytest cases in test_new_features.py — 13/15 pass. Two failures on /api/value/undervalued expose a CRITICAL semantics bug: mode=undervalued returns players with ratio (pred/actual) < 1 (i.e. overvalued) and mode=overvalued returns ratio > 1 — the sort direction is inverted vs the review spec and vs the UI labels/verdicts. Frontend: /compare, /value, /nations all render correctly. Direct-link /compare?a=158023&b=20801 shows Messi vs Ronaldo, wins 15-13, radar and 29-row attribute table. Search + swap + clear work. Value page KPIs (R²=0.981, N=17,907), what-if simulator, bargain radar with mode toggle, model coefficients table and scatter all render. Nations page renders green choropleth, metric toggles work, Brazil/UK country clicks open panel; UK correctly shows 'Includes England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland'. Compare drawer flow via player profile modal works: add-to-compare → drawer shows slot-0, second player → slot-1 + go-compare-btn, drawer persists across reload (localStorage), compare-now-btn navigates to /compare with both players, remove/clear buttons work. Navbar nav-compare/value/nations visible at 1920px; hamburger + mnav-* visible at 1024px. Regression on /, /explorer, /statistics: pages load with zero pageerrors.

critical.issue: Mode semantics inverted. `mode=undervalued` returns rows where `ratio = predicted/actual < 1` (actual market price > model fair value → OVERVALUED). `mode=overvalued` returns `ratio > 1` (UNDERVALUED). Root cause: server.py line 799 `resid.sort_values(ascending=(mode != 'undervalued'))`. With residual = log(actual)-log(pred), an undervalued player (market cheap) has residual < 0. So mode='undervalued' must sort ASCENDING. Fix: change to `ascending=(mode == 'undervalued')`. This bug also flips the UI 'Bargain radar' table meaning — Cristiano Ronaldo/Messi (ratio 4.6 / 4.1) appear as top 'Overvalued' when they are model-implied undervalued vs their FIFA-listed value.

minor.issue: No diacritic normalization. q='Kante' returns 0 results because dataset has 'N. Kanté'. Placeholder text on /value literally suggests 'Kanté' — user typing plain ASCII gets nothing. Recommend unicodedata.normalize('NFKD') fold on both sides.

ui_bugs.issue: Because it consumes /api/value/undervalued directly, the 'Undervalued' vs 'Overvalued' tabs are swapped in the UI. On page load 'Undervalued' shows overvalued stars (Ronaldo, Messi with 4x ratio) and vice-versa. Blocks intended feature until backend bug is fixed.

rca of the issue: value_undervalued (server.py:788-800) sorts by log-residual. VALUE_RESID is computed as log(actual) - log(predicted) (confirmed empirically: N. Kanté ratio 0.24 → residual 1.42 = ln(160000/38507)). A player is 'undervalued' in the marketing sense when actual < predicted, i.e. residual < 0. Current code: `ascending=(mode != 'undervalued')` → for mode='undervalued' this is False (descending), returning MAX residual = MAX(log(actual/pred)) = players whose market price GREATLY EXCEEDS the model = OVERVALUED. Reproduction: `curl '$BASE/api/value/undervalued?mode=undervalued&limit=1'` returns O. Pérez ratio 0.24 (pred/actual). Fix: flip the boolean → `ascending=(mode == 'undervalued')`.
